steps.title: Prepare 18 mm coverslips
steps.instruction: Four days before culture, clean, acid‑treat, dry‑heat, coat with gelatine, paraffin, UV‑sterilize and apply poly‑L‑lysine to 18 mm coverslips.

substeps.instruction: Rinse 18 mm coverslips in Milli‑Q water and place in custom racks.
Immerse racks in 63 % nitric acid for 12 h.
Rinse twice with Milli‑Q water for 2 h each.
Dry on 12.5 cm filter paper and sterilize by dry heat at 200 °C for 10–12 h.
Transfer five coverslips per 60 mm plastic Petri dish; add 10 µL of 1 % sterile‑filtered gelatine solution to each to keep them in place.
Using a glass Pasteur pipette with suction, move coverslips to the dish.
Melt sterile paraffin to 150 °C in a PTFE dish; apply three small drops to each coverslip with a fire‑polished Pasteur pipette (tip tip‑bead ≈2 mm, bent 50°–80° about 3 cm from tip).
UV‑irradiate coverslips for 30 min in a class II biosafety cabinet.
Spray poly‑L‑lysine solution onto coverslips with a 1.5 mL miniature spray bottle, positioning the dish ≈5 cm below the nozzle; let droplets settle by gravity.
Let the poly‑L‑lysine dry at room temperature overnight.
Rinse coverslips twice with sterile Milli‑Q water for 2 h each.
Add 4 mL neuronal plating medium to each dish, place in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator, and replace the medium with fresh plating medium before cell plating.

steps.title: Dissect embryonic hippocampi
steps.instruction: Harvest hippocampi from E16‑E17 mouse embryos, keep tissues cold, and prepare for dissociation.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize a timed‑pregnant BALB/c mouse by cervical dislocation and place the uterus in a sterile 10 cm Petri dish.
Remove fetuses, decapitate with scissors, and place heads in HBSS kept at 4 °C.
Under a dissecting microscope, extract brains, separate hemispheres, strip meninges, and isolate hippocampi.
Transfer all hippocampi from one litter into a 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Enzymatic dissociation of hippocampi
steps.instruction: Treat hippocampi with trypsin, wash, and mechanically triturate to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm all media and reagents to 37 °C.
Add HBSS to a total volume of 4.5 mL and then add 0.5 mL 2.5 % trypsin (10×).
Incubate 15 min at 37 °C in a water bath.
Remove trypsin, add 5 mL HBSS, let stand 5 min; repeat twice, ending with a final volume of 3 mL (or 4 mL if >5 brains).
Gently triturate with a fire‑polished Pasteur pipette (first half‑diameter, then quarter‑diameter) about 7–8 times until no tissue chunks remain.

steps.title: Count and plate hippocampal neurons
steps.instruction: Determine cell density and seed neurons onto the prepared coverslips.

substeps.instruction: Count cells using a Neubauer hemacytometer.
Add 25 000 cells to each dish containing poly‑L‑lysine‑treated coverslips in neuronal plating medium (≈880 cells cm⁻²).

steps.title: Optional lentiviral infection
steps.instruction: Introduce lentiviral particles to achieve ~50 % transduction.

substeps.instruction: Add lentiviral suspension (≤1 mL per dish containing 4 mL plating medium) to the freshly plated neurons; volume and concentration should be empirically determined to reach ~50 % infection.

steps.title: Transfer neurons to astroglial feeder
steps.instruction: After 3 h, move coverslips with attached neurons onto astroglial feeder dishes.

substeps.instruction: Using forceps, lift each coverslip and place it upside‑down into a dish containing astroglial cells bathed in neuronal maintenance medium.

steps.title: Control glial proliferation
steps.instruction: Add Ara‑C to limit glial growth.

substeps.instruction: Three days after plating, add Ara‑C to a final concentration of 5 µM.
Once per week, remove 2 mL of neuronal maintenance medium and replace with 2 mL of fresh medium.

steps.title: Prepare astroglial feeder layer
steps.instruction: Generate a confluent astroglial monolayer 14 days before hippocampal plating.

substeps.instruction: Mince brain hemispheres (from the same or additional embryos) with Vannas‑Tübingen spring scissors.
Transfer minced tissue to a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 12 mL HBSS.
Add 1.5 mL 1 % DNase solution; incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Add 1.5 mL 2.5 % trypsin (10×); incubate 15 min at 37 °C, triturating gently every 5 min with a 5 mL serological pipette (7–8 strokes).
Add 3 mL horse serum to stop trypsin activity.
Filter the suspension through a 72 µm nylon mesh.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 200 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; resuspend the pellet in 5 mL glial medium.
Count cells and seed 4 × 10⁶ cells into a 75 cm² T‑flask; bring the volume to 13 mL with glial medium.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Day 3: replace glial medium completely with fresh medium.
Day 7: shake the flask vigorously (slap 2–3 times on a hard surface) to dislodge microglia; replace medium with fresh glial medium.
When the flask reaches 70–80 % confluence (~10 days), wash with 10 mL HBSS, add 10 mL 0.5 % trypsin‑EDTA (in HBSS), and incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Tap gently, add 1 mL horse serum, and allow cells to detach; collect the suspension, centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet in 40 mL glial medium.
Plate 4 mL of this glial suspension into each 60 mm Primaria plastic Petri dish.
Incubate dishes at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Next day: replace glial medium with fresh glial medium.
One day before hippocampal plating (day 3 of this schedule), replace glial medium with 6 mL neuronal maintenance medium and return dishes to the incubator.

steps.title: Record action potentials from WT neuron
steps.instruction: Obtain a single‑cell action potential waveform to use as a stimulation template.

substeps.instruction: Pull a glass patch pipette (3–5 mm short taper) and fire‑polish the tip; final resistance should be 2–4 MΩ when filled with intracellular solution.
Place a coverslip with WT neurons in the low‑profile recording chamber and add 300 µL extracellular solution.
Patch the neuron with probe 1 in voltage‑clamp mode, hold at –70 mV, then switch to current‑clamp mode.
Record spontaneous activity; if none is observed, inject 5 pA current and increase in 5 pA steps until action potentials appear.
Export a representative action potential as a stimulation template file named “Stim_1.tpl” (store in the PatchMaster program folder).

steps.title: Single‑stimulus paired‑neuron recording
steps.instruction: Stimulate one neuron while recording the postsynaptic response from its partner.

substeps.instruction: Pull two patch pipettes as above (2–4 MΩ).
Place the paired‑neuron coverslip in the chamber and add 300 µL extracellular solution.
Patch both neurons (probe 1 and probe 2) in voltage‑clamp mode, hold each at –70 mV.
Load stimulation protocol “Stim‑1” for probe 1 (presynaptic) and record Vmon‑1 and Imon‑2; then load “Stim‑2” for the opposite configuration.
Ensure the corresponding template file (Stim_1.tpl or Stim_2.tpl) is present in the PatchMaster directory.

steps.title: Paired‑pulse stimulation
steps.instruction: Apply a paired‑pulse protocol to assess short‑term synaptic plasticity.

substeps.instruction: Create a protocol that delivers two depolarizations from –70 mV to +60 mV, each 5 ms long, with a variable inter‑pulse interval.
Apply this protocol to the presynaptic cell (probe 1) while recording from the postsynaptic cell (probe 2), then repeat with the roles reversed.
